subject: PrivEnv architecture review — propose 60‑minute deep dive and slots

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivEnv architecture review — propose 60‑minute deep dive and slots

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks again for the discovery call this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Goal: run a Private/VPC deployment of Redwood for inference (model hosting + telemetry) with strict egress controls and customer‑managed KMS.
- Key constraints you mentioned: single VPC peering, no cross‑tenant routing, retention rules for logs, and desire for private peering to avoid public egress.

To make the next meeting productive, we suggest a 60‑minute architecture review + tech deep dive where our solutions engineer will walk the proposed network pattern, KMS integration, and deployment options (on‑prem appliance vs. VPC private control plane). Please confirm who from your infra/security team will join.

Proposed slots (all PT):
- Tue 2027‑06‑07 09:00–10:00
- Tue 2027‑06‑07 14:00–15:00
- Wed 2027‑06‑08 11:00–12:00

Attached: RWI‑privenv‑overview.pdf (short explainer) and soc2‑dataflow‑diagram.png. If none of the above work, tell me a couple of windows that do and we’ll align.

Prep items we recommend you share ahead of the call: 1) VPC CIDR(s) and peering topology, 2) egress/firewall rules, 3) preferred KMS provider and key rotation policy. This will let us tailor the session.

Thanks — I’ll hold the times on my calendar tentatively until you confirm.

— Stephanie

Alex / Priya — looping in with a short tech note before the call.

High level we support:
- Object store (S3/GCS) as the recommended primary artifact store (preferred for scalability & integrity).
- We can also run a mounted POSIX filesystem for model artifacts in private deployments but it requires an NFS gateway and adds operational complexity (locks, backup windows).

Pre‑call asks (if possible):
- VPC CIDR(s) + peering target IP(s)
- Any IP allowlist or proxy in front of outbound egress
- A sample retention policy for audit logs (days)

Proposed walkthrough bullets for the call:
- Network flows (control plane vs runtime data plane)
- KMS integration and envelope encryption flow
- Artifact store tradeoffs and backup strategy
- Monitoring/trace collection and where logs land (customer bucket vs RWI managed sink)

If you can drop the CIDRs into the Drive folder, I’ll annotate the diagram before the session.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
